title: Proofs in Mathematics

sections.heading: Conditionals and Related Statements
bullets: Statement p → q; converse q → p; inverse ¬p → ¬q; contrapositive ¬q → ¬p.
A statement and its contrapositive are logically equivalent; converse and inverse are equivalent to each other but not to the original.
Example: "If it rains, the road is wet" → contrapositive "If the road is not wet, it did not rain".
Quantifiers: "for all" is disproved by one counterexample; "there exists" is proved by one example.

sections.heading: Quick Proofs
sections.body: Even + even: 2a + 2b = 2(a + b), even. Induction base n = 1: 1 = 1·2/2 true; step: add (k + 1) to k(k + 1)/2 to get (k + 1)(k + 2)/2.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Mathematical proofs use logical deduction; the main styles are direct, contrapositive, contradiction, induction and counterexample.
keyFacts: One counterexample kills a universal claim.

highYieldFacts: √2 irrational is the standard contradiction proof.
commonTraps: Do not treat the converse as proof of the original.
